verdict.rationale: Cline is itself an AI coding assistant built into the editor and CLI. Its docs describe delegating tasks such as creating files, running commands and browsing, with Plan/Act modes, optional auto-approve for autonomous execution, and subagents. Hands-on community reports confirm users plan with it, then set it loose on their codebase and get accurate diffs back.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: AI coding assistant in your editor. Create files, run commands, browse the web, and use tools with human-in-the-loop approval.
It can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser, and help you build features through natural conversation.
Toggle Plan mode to align on a strategy, then Act to execute. Approve every step, or flip auto-approve for autopilot.
Autonomous execution can modify files and run commands without further prompts.
I can plan with it for 10-15 minutes, set it loose on my codebase, go get lunch, and then its diff is almost always completely on the money.
